newsitem.title: POLAND: Newspaper says Poland's Kolodko to quit.
newsitem.headline: Newspaper says Poland's Kolodko to quit.

text.p: Poland's Zycie Warszawy daily reported on Monday that Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko was about to quit, but Kolodko said he would himself decide when to leave the cabinet and he would inform the media then.
The Warsaw newspaper said Kolodko had long quarrelled with Prime Minister Wlodzimierz Cimoszewicz and had now also lost the support of his hitherto backer, President Aleksander Kwasniewski.

Quoting an unnamed source close to the prime minister, Zycie Warszawy said Kolodko would submit his resignation on Tuesday and this would be accepted, while discussions were already underway with a potential successor.

Kolodko, interviewed by Polish public radio at the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland, said reporters should ask the prime minister and president if they were willing to continue working with him or not.
But he added: "I once said...that I and only I will decide whether I am going to leave the government."
"The moment that my mission is completed I will state this and will ask the media and journalists to convey this to public opinion," Kolodko said.
Kolodko recalled repeated previous speculation about his departure, and noted Poland's economic performance since he became finance minister in 1994.
The government's spokeswoman and a close aide to President Kwasniewski both declined to comment on the Zycie Warszawy report.
Kolodko, who also holds the title of deputy prime minister, is a non-party academic close to the ex-communists turned social democrats who dominate Poland's coalition government.

He is widely credited internationally for having continued many of the market reforms launched after the 1989 fall of communism by governments rooted in the Solidarity movement, and he has authored Poland's medium-term economic strategy aimed at maintaining economic growth while reducing inflation.

He has been involved in repeated controversies with other ministers and the central bank, and his ministry's authority was effectively reduced during a reorganisation of cabinet portfolios begun late last year.

Last month he had a public row with Agriculture Minister Roman Jagielinski of the Polish Peasant Party (PSL), the smaller partner in the coalition, who wished to restore import duties on grain, which had been suspended because of high prices.
Duties on grain for livestock feed were restored despite Kolodko's protests that this would boost inflation, and he publicly criticised the cabinet decision.
